caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This grouped bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, comparing six model configurations: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red/pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). The horizontal axis is labeled "family" and contains nine language family categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled "effect" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately 0 to 30, with tick marks at 0, 10, 20, and 30. Each language family group contains six bars arranged side by side in the order listed in the legend, and each bar includes error bars indicating standard deviation. For IE-Baltic, all six bars are relatively small, ranging from roughly 1 to 5. In IE-Germanic, the bars are moderate, with mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ near 10, mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ near 0–1, and mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ reaching approximately 15 and 15 respectively. IE-Indic shows the tallest bars overall, with mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ around 18 and 17, mBERT-B₂ near 24, and XLM-B₂ near 21, while the L₂ variants are much smaller at roughly 1–2. IE-Romance bars are moderate, with values generally between 1 and 13. IE-Slavic shows the B₂ variants reaching approximately 17 and 10, while L₂ and R₂ variants are smaller, around 5–9. IE-other has bars ranging from about 5 to 8. Isolate shows near-zero effects across all configurations. Semitic displays notable variability with very wide error bars; mBERT-L₂ reaches approximately 11, while some bars such as mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ appear slightly negative. Uralic shows near-zero effects for most configurations, though XLM-B₂ reaches approximately 19 with a very large error bar. The bars are not sorted by value but rather grouped by language family in a fixed order, and no bars appear visually emphasized beyond the color coding and error bars.
